title: Sampling inventory + dashboard migration notes
content:
Purpose / context:
Quick capture of the work-in-progress runbook for spanning sampling inventory and the dashboard migration we discussed in today's observability sync. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — notes, experiment outcomes, open questions, and a prioritized action list for the next two sprints.

Meeting snapshot (2028-06-12, 10:30–11:15):
- Focus: align on which services need aggressive sampling changes this quarter, and plan the migration of the long-running cost/dashboards to the new templating layer.
- Outcome: agreed on a phased sampling rollout + dashboard cutover plan; validated one small experiment with heap of numbers below.

Key context:
- Background: span volume continues to grow ~18% q/q; our current uniform sampling policy wastes signals on low-value internal flows and balloons storage/ingest costs.
- Constraint: sampling should not remove rare-service error signals that trigger alerts; dashboards must remain stable for support and SRE runbooks.

Inventory summary (quick):
- High-volume candidates (noisy): auth-proxy, metrics-ingest, tokenizer-worker — collectively ~45% of spans.
- Mid-volume: api-gateway, routing, model-serve (per-model frontends).
- Low-volume but high-significance: billing, audit-log, webhooks.
- Current global sampler: 1.0 for errors, 0.05 for traces by default.

Experiment run: adaptive-latency-bucket-sampling (proof-of-concept)
- Hypothesis: increase sampling on high-latency traces (p95 > 280ms) and reduce sampling on low-latency traces results in better signal-to-cost ratio while preserving alert fidelity.
- Implementation: short patch in ingestion pipeline (branch: sampling/latency-buckets). Decision logic: if p95_bucket >= 280ms then sampling_rate = max(0.2, 4x baseline); else sampling_rate = baseline * 0.5 for requests < 50ms. Errors were still forced-sampled.
- Window: 72 hours on canary subset (10% of traffic) for three critical services: api-gateway, model-serve, auth-proxy.
- Result summary:
  - api-gateway: span ingest down 36%, retained 92% of alerting error traces, CPU for collector reduced by ~12%.
  - model-serve: span ingest down 29%, observed a small uptick (1.3x) in rare timeout traces captured (good), cost estimate for storage reduced by ~27%.
  - auth-proxy: overall reduction 48%, but missed 2 low-frequency auth-failure sequences — flagged as a risk.
- Quick takeaway: adaptive-latency sampling shows promise; needs additional safeties for low-frequency but important errors.

Dashboard migration notes (templating layer v2):
- Goal: migrate the cost, span-volume, and alert-stability dashboards to templated dashboards so teams can swap service / time window without re-creating panels.
- Roadblocks identified:
  1) Some panels use undocumented PromQL joins that v2 templating cannot express yet.
  2) Panel ownership is unclear — several dashboards used by both SRE and platform eng.
  3) Existing data model expects raw span count; after sampling rollout we will need normalized counts / effective-sample-rate columns.
- Plan:
  - Phase 1 (this sprint): create templated skeletons for the 3 canonical dashboards (cost, span-volume, alert-latency). Keep original dashboards live as read-only copies.
  - Phase 2 (next sprint): migrate 5 high-use panels and convert their queries to use normalized counts (formula: observed_count / effective_sample_rate).
  - Phase 3 (post-sampling rollout): toggle panels to point at sampled-normalized views and decommission old raw-count panels.

Open questions / safety checks:
- What threshold do we use to mark a service as "low-frequency important" so it gets an exception and remains at higher sampling? (Proposal: services with <1000 requests/day that serve billing/audit endpoints should default to 1.0 sampling.)
- How to best surface effective_sample_rate in existing dashboards (API or precomputed metric)? Precompute recommended for performance.
- Rollback triggers: define clear SLO-based rollback rules (e.g., if error-detection rate falls below 0.95 baseline for three consecutive days, revert sampling for that service).

Action items (owner — due):
- Aisha: write short RFC for the adaptive-latency sampling heuristic with exception list proposal (due 2028-06-19).
- Mateo: instrument and precompute effective_sample_rate metric in telemetry pipeline; add to metrics catalog (linked PR in repo) (due 2028-06-26).
- Lina: build templated dashboard skeletons and add migration checklist; tag panel owners in the doc (due 2028-06-19).
- Omar: add automated canary monitor that compares alert-detection rate between baseline and sampled cohorts (PoC) (due 2028-06-26).
- Becky: run a manual audit of low-volume services and propose exception list (due 2028-06-16).

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: missing rare but critical traces (mitigate: exception list + forced-sampling for all spans with error flag).
- Risk: dashboard divergence during migration (mitigate: read-only snapshot + dual-writing to templated view for two weeks).
- Risk: unexpected cost pulse on migration due to mis-normalization (mitigate: cost smoke test against staging rollouts).

Notes to follow up in next sync (2028-06-19):
- Review Aisha's RFC + Becky’s exception list.
- Check status of effective_sample_rate metric and initial dashboard skeleton.
- Decide canary cohort expansion to 25% if PoC monitors look healthy.

Quick links & refs:
- OBS-512 (sampling playbook): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OBS-512
- PR for sampling POC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/796
- Confluence: Observability/Sampling-Playbook-v2

Fragmented notes / reminders (informal):
- consider a per-service budget guardrail tag so product teams can opt-in for higher fidelity (cost owner = product).
- internal note: Jonah will try the sampler on a high-cardinality internal header scenario next week (watch for cardinality explosion).
- keep default error force-sample across all environments.

Status: in_review — please comment on confluence RFC draft or ping Aisha/Becky in #observability.
